import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
T = 15                         # number of weeks
lead_time = 3                  # weeks between order and receipt
initial_stock = 69             # units on hand at start of week 1
stock_capacity = 69            # maximum inventory that can be stored
order_min = 19                 # minimum order size each week
order_max = 57                 # maximum order size each week
procurement_cost = 2           # cost per unit ordered
holding_cost = 3               # cost per unit of inventory carried to next week
shortage_penalty = 15          # penalty per unit of unmet demand
demand = [22, 20, 35, 13, 60, 59, 31, 58, 53, 43,
          22, 56, 30, 21, 43]  # weekly demand (weeks 1 … 15)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("procurement_stock_plan", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
order = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "order",
    (t for t in range(1, T + 1)),
    lowBound=order_min,
    upBound=order_max,
    cat="Continuous",
)

stock = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "stock",
    (t for t in range(0, T + 1)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=stock_capacity,
    cat="Continuous",
)

shortage = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "shortage",
    (t for t in range(1, T + 1)),
    lowBound=0,
    cat="Continuous",
)

receive = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "receive",
    (t for t in range(1, T + 1)),
    lowBound=0,
    cat="Continuous",
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Initial inventory
model += stock[0] == initial_stock, "initial_stock"

# Receipt definition (orders arrive after lead_time weeks)
for t in range(1, T + 1):
    if t <= lead_time:
        model += receive[t] == 0, f"receive_zero_{t}"
    else:
        model += receive[t] == order[t - lead_time], f"receive_def_{t}"

# Inventory balance for each week
for t in range(1, T + 1):
    model += (
        stock[t - 1] + receive[t] - demand[t - 1] + shortage[t] == stock[t],
        f"balance_{t}",
    )

# Shortage cannot exceed demand of the week
for t in range(1, T + 1):
    model += shortage[t] <= demand[t - 1], f"shortage_ub_{t}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize total cost (procurement + holding + shortage penalty)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
procurement = pulp.lpSum(procurement_cost * order[t] for t in range(1, T + 1))
holding = pulp.lpSum(holding_cost * stock[t] for t in range(0, T))  # inventory carried to next week
penalty = pulp.lpSum(shortage_penalty * shortage[t] for t in range(1, T + 1))

model += procurement + holding + penalty, "total_cost"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print(f"Total cost = {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}\n")
print("Week |  Order | Receive | Stock_end | Shortage")
print("-" * 48)
for t in range(1, T + 1):
    o = order[t].varValue
    r = receive[t].varValue
    s = stock[t].varValue
    sh = shortage[t].varValue
    print(f"{t:4d} | {o:6.2f} | {r:7.2f} | {s:9.2f} | {sh:8.2f}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Minimum‑pallet loading problem solved with PuLP and the HiGHS solver.

Each cargo piece must be placed on exactly one pallet.
The total mass on any pallet cannot exceed 100 kg.
The goal is to minimise the number of pallets used.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
items = [
    "Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon", "Zeta", "Eta", "Theta",
    "Iota", "Kappa", "Lambda", "Mu", "Nu", "Xi", "Omicron", "Pi", "Rho", "Sigma"
]

mass = {
    "Alpha":   45,
    "Beta":    41,
    "Gamma":   45,
    "Delta":   31,
    "Epsilon": 40,
    "Zeta":    65,
    "Eta":     40,
    "Theta":   35,
    "Iota":    57,
    "Kappa":   68,
    "Lambda":  36,
    "Mu":      69,
    "Nu":      70,
    "Xi":      59,
    "Omicron": 39,
    "Pi":      69,
    "Rho":     68,
    "Sigma":   32
}

capacity = 100          # kg per pallet
max_pallets = len(items)  # an upper bound (one pallet per item)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("MinPallets", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[i,p] = 1 if item i is placed on pallet p
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, p) for i in items for p in range(max_pallets)),
    cat=pulp.LpBinary
)

# y[p] = 1 if pallet p is used
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    (p for p in range(max_pallets)),
    cat=pulp.LpBinary
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise the number of pallets used
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(y[p] for p in range(max_pallets)), "TotalPalletsUsed"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Each item must be assigned to exactly one pallet
for i in items:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, p)] for p in range(max_pallets)) == 1,
        f"Assign_{i}"
    )

# 2) Capacity of each pallet cannot be exceeded
for p in range(max_pallets):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(mass[i] * x[(i, p)] for i in items) <= capacity * y[p],
        f"Capacity_{p}"
    )

# 3) Linking: a pallet can be used only if at least one item is placed on it
for i in items:
    for p in range(max_pallets):
        model += (
            x[(i, p)] <= y[p],
            f"Link_{i}_{p}"
        )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    used_pallets = [p for p in range(max_pallets) if pulp.value(y[p]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Minimum number of pallets required: {len(used_pallets)}\n")

    # Build a readable assignment
    assignment = {p: [] for p in used_pallets}
    for i in items:
        for p in used_pallets:
            if pulp.value(x[(i, p)]) > 0.5:
                assignment[p].append(i)
                break

    for p in sorted(assignment):
        pallet_items = assignment[p]
        total_mass = sum(mass[i] for i in pallet_items)
        print(f"Pallet {p + 1}:")
        print(f"  Items ({len(pallet_items)}): {', '.join(pallet_items)}")
        print(f"  Total mass: {total_mass} kg\n")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Routes: each entry is a list of (center, duration) for the 4 stages
routes = {
    1: [("C2", 3), ("C3", 5), ("C4", 1), ("C1", 1)],
    2: [("C1", 6), ("C4", 10), ("C2", 1), ("C3", 10)],
    3: [("C4", 6), ("C3", 9), ("C2", 3), ("C1", 4)],
    4: [("C4", 3), ("C3", 3), ("C2", 5), ("C1", 6)]
}

# Big‑M value – larger than any possible makespan
M = 100

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("logistics_schedule", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Start‑time variables S[(r,k)]  (r = route, k = stage)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "S",
    [(r, k) for r in routes for k in range(1, 5)],
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous
)

# Makespan
C_max = pulp.LpVariable("C_max", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Precedence constraints (within each route)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for r, stages in routes.items():
    for k in range(1, 4):          # stages 1‑3 must precede the next one
        dur = stages[k - 1][1]     # duration of stage k
        model += (
            S[(r, k + 1)] >= S[(r, k)] + dur,
            f"prec_route{r}_stage{k}_to_{k+1}"
        )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Makespan definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for r, stages in routes.items():
    last_dur = stages[3][1]          # duration of stage 4
    model += (
        C_max >= S[(r, 4)] + last_dur,
        f"makespan_route{r}"
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Binary ordering variables for operations sharing the same center
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build a flat list of operations with their attributes
ops = []   # each element: (id, route, stage, center, duration)
for r, stages in routes.items():
    for k, (center, dur) in enumerate(stages, start=1):
        ops.append(((r, k), r, k, center, dur))

# Helper to retrieve operation data by its id
op_dict = {op_id: {"center": center, "duration": dur}
           for op_id, _, _, center, dur in ops}

# Create binary variables X[(i,j)] for each unordered pair sharing a center
X = {}
for i in range(len(ops)):
    id_i = ops[i][0]
    center_i = op_dict[id_i]["center"]
    dur_i = op_dict[id_i]["duration"]
    for j in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
        id_j = ops[j][0]
        center_j = op_dict[id_j]["center"]
        dur_j = op_dict[id_j]["duration"]
        if center_i == center_j:          # same distribution center → need ordering
            var_name = f"X_{id_i[0]}_{id_i[1]}_before_{id_j[0]}_{id_j[1]}"
            X[(id_i, id_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

            # If X = 1 → i before j
            model += (
                S[id_j] >= S[id_i] + dur_i - M * (1 - X[(id_i, id_j)]),
                f"order_{id_i}_before_{id_j}"
            )
            # If X = 0 → j before i
            model += (
                S[id_i] >= S[id_j] + dur_j - M * X[(id_i, id_j)],
                f"order_{id_j}_before_{id_i}"
            )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += C_max, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (C_max): {pulp.value(C_max)}\n")

print("Start times for each route stage:")
for r in sorted(routes):
    for k in range(1, 5):
        start = pulp.value(S[(r, k)])
        center, dur = routes[r][k - 1]
        print(f"  Route {r}, Stage {k} (Center {center}, Dur {dur}) -> Start = {start}")

# (Optional) show ordering decisions
print("\nOrdering decisions on shared centers:")
for (i, j), var in X.items():
    order = pulp.value(var)
    if order is not None:
        print(f"  Operation {i} before {j}: {int(order)}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Optimization model for selecting conservation practices on agricultural fields
to achieve a required reduction in nutrient runoff at minimum cost.

The model uses PuLP with the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Number of fields and practices
n_fields = 9
n_practices = 9

# Runoff coefficients (unitless) – not directly needed because baseline runoff is given
coeff = [
    1.139, 1.837, 0.621, 2.987, 2.155,
    2.134, 0.549, 2.224, 1.542
]

# Cultivated area of each field (ha)
area = [
    145.063, 186.821, 168.599, 88.282, 223.798,
    207.578, 125.279, 215.416, 215.621
]

# Baseline nutrient runoff for each field (kg N)
baseline_runoff = [
    165.229, 343.191, 104.699, 263.698, 482.285,
    442.971, 68.777, 479.087, 332.49
]

# Reduction efficacy of each practice (fraction of nutrient loss removed)
reduction = [
    0.68, 0.42, 0.79, 0.24, 0.82,
    0.32, 0.81, 0.81, 0.82
]

# Cost per hectare for each (field, practice) pair (currency/ha)
cost_per_area = [
    [47.743, 47.952, 59.969, 109.398, 48.318, 143.653, 66.117, 17.487, 104.307],
    [49.462, 187.294, 72.815, 10.52, 137.61, 182.307, 168.694, 137.114, 38.337],
    [27.116, 107.224, 147.477, 29.245, 58.619, 53.92, 197.847, 66.244, 98.213],
    [28.964, 43.193, 17.494, 65.208, 162.303, 69.414, 150.323, 28.05, 154.059],
    [18.719, 171.88, 136.037, 42.397, 77.93, 93.166, 128.143, 176.91, 27.661],
    [164.843, 44.745, 86.148, 192.839, 61.648, 83.286, 171.628, 161.981, 133.281],
    [161.413, 31.481, 142.272, 21.143, 189.069, 40.285, 89.045, 122.243, 162.43],
    [138.895, 44.44, 82.153, 78.134, 15.475, 140.048, 169.322, 194.954, 34.825],
    [184.876, 31.458, 88.144, 18.735, 59.706, 69.705, 143.868, 138.806, 155.83]
]

# Required proportion of total baseline runoff that must be reduced
P = 0.488

# Total baseline runoff (kg N) – also provided directly
total_baseline_runoff = 2682.427

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Nutrient_Runoff_Reduction", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: a[i,p] = 1 if practice p is adopted on field i, else 0
a = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "a",
    ((i, p) for i in range(n_fields) for p in range(n_practices)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
